Bringing together sculpture, drawing and live action, the exhibition will take the form of an immersive installation. Made in collaboration with LGBTQIA+ communities in and around Manchester, Vitalities explores queer grief and houses, amongst other artworks, eight luminescent sculptures created in workshops with people who have experienced grief as a process of reflection and catharsis. The exhibition is free to attend but you have to book a slot online, there’s also going to be fortnightly live activations, with dancers taking over the space. Interested in more events? evidence_packet.evidence_text: Harvest Celebrations at Platt Fields Market Garden - Manchester’s Finest Harvest Celebrations at Platt Fields Market Garden Sat 17th Oct, 2026 - Platt Fields Market Garden c: Jody Hartley Harvest Celebrations at Platt Fields Market Garden Platt Fields Market Garden, Platt Fields Market Garden, Platt Fields Park, Fallowfield, Manchester M14 6LT Sat 17th Oct, 2026 10am - 6pm From £5 Get tickets Directions events Go to Manchester's Finest Facebook page Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A glorious annual celebration of harvest season, Platt Fields Market sees local artist Jasmin Issaka hold a number of creative workshops this year, for all ages resulting in a ‘play in a day’. There’ll be set building, costume creating and performance workshops between 10-4 with a performance held at the end of the day at 5pm. There’ll also be a seasonal feast for both the performers and attendees. MUD Kitchen and ARMR will host a lunch for those involved in the workshops and a dinner for attendees of the play to tuck into after the show. It’s all being held in conjunction with wildly on-trend perfumery Ffern , as part of their Folk Foundation initiative, supporting the new generation of British folk arts and traditions. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Last confirmed: 10 September 2026 Event date: 2026-10-11 Venue: Bolton Car Boot Sale Price: £1 Status: https://schema.org/EventScheduled

Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Witches and Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours and explores what it means to be a witch today. Themes explored include wellbeing, aging and place in relation to magic, healing and ritual offering an unparalleled insight into the diverse lives of women who live as witches and healers. Through a feminist lens Hillman uses a mixture of moving image and photography to explore menopause, mental health, outsider identities and sisterhood as well as how women imagine a better world through ritual and magic. Completely free to attend and running until February 2027, drop by to see the exhibition or book in for one of the accompanying workshops or film screenings throughout its run. Trafford Council has granted planning permission for BeKind Care Ltd to transform the former Honeybear Nursery at 160-160A Moss Lane, close to the junction with Sandileigh Avenue. The facility will provide planned and emergency short breaks and overnight care for up to five children and young people under the age of 18. evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

Revnu was founded by George Jefferson and Art Freebrey, who first met in secondary school before going on to launch a string of businesses together while still in education. A northern engineering base The software belongs to bet365, founded in 2000 in North Staffordshire. By 2023 it employed more than 6,000 people and operated in 21 languages, figures the company gave when its technology arm, Hillside Technology, set up a Platform Innovation Hub to test new tools against the core platform. Manchester came first, in 2016. The firm opened its first satellite technology office in Spring Gardens, hiring 50 to 70 people to support the development teams in Stoke-on-Trent. Dom Hawley, then head of software development, said at the time that bet365 had found exceptional people in Stoke but now had to recruit outside the local area to keep growing. BusinessCloud covered the move into Manchester when it was announced. A year later the Spring Gardens office was set to grow from 60 to more than 150 staff , with developers in both cities building the HTML5 desktop site together. Testing followed. The agreement will enable THG Fulfil to offer AutoStore systems through both traditional CapEx ownership and its existing Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model. The expanded partnership gives brands and retailers greater commercial flexibility when investing in warehouse automation. Businesses will be able to select CapEx, RaaS or a hybrid of the two to match their investment strategy without changing their distribution and integration partner. THG Fulfil currently operates 796 AutoStore robots across its own fulfilment network and has integrated the AutoStore system with its proprietary warehouse control system (WCS). The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The work comes in addition to the programme of repairs already agreed for the borough this year and is possible following a £5m cash injection from the Greater Man Of that money, almost £4m will be split between the 23 key routes lined up for resurfacing, which is expected to take place in the next 12 months. Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 05:53, 15 Oct 2026 Updated 07:05, 15 Oct 202 A visitor to Manchester says he has been left 'helpless' and 'homeless' after his luxury city centre studio became infested with bedbugs The man, who asked to remain anonymous, told the Manchester Evening News of a nightmare experience at a flat in the Swan Street House complex in the Northern Quarter . A medical professional and originally from Birmingham, he travelled to work an study in the city After a fortnight in the region, he decided to book himself a short stay at the deluxe high-rise on Mason Street. He told the MEN his 12-day stay cost £1,634 when he booked it online. But after just one evening, he claims to have woke up with bug bites all over his body The property is understood to have offered the individual a refund since the incident. He said: "After the first day, I got a few rashes on my body so I went to the housekeeping and they came and changed my bedding "The second night it was more obvious, I thought there was something that doesn't look right. I called the housekeeping again and they did the same thing. But I wasn't convinced, I thought there was something more than that. So, I removed the mattress and it was full of bedbugs."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Apple Watch text that changed a family's life forever "All I have left of the last 20 years of my life is her" View 4 Images Clair Fitzharris and son Sam Fitzharris (Image: Greater Manchester Police) Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 05:59, 09 Oct 2026 It was a drizzly, cold afternoon on December 23, 2023. Martin Fitzharris was busy building his nephew a PC for Christmas . He was expecting his partner, Clair Fitzharris, son, Sam, and 13-year-old daughter Instead, he received a text that changed his life forever. Clair's Apple Watch, which had him as a named emergency contact, sent him a message to say they had been involved in a collision Within seconds of getting that text he relentlessly tried to call each of them who had been in that car that afternoon, with no success. Eventually someone answered Clair's phone, but it wasn't Clair It was sadly too late. Clair, 42, and Sam, 15, had been killed . His daughter had been left with life-changing injuries that still require surgery to this day Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Andrew Hall had collided with their Nissan on Ripponden Road, Oldham , after veering onto the opposite side of the road. He had been travelling at over 90mph, and overtaken over cards, and braked three seconds before the crash

Coun Yusuf Davda recently topped the poll in a by-election for Rumworth ward on July 30 as an Independent He gained 1.458 votes with Labour in second on 1,054. The Greens were third in the poll, with their candidate Alan Johnson getting 517 votes Coun Davda said: “Over recent months, it has become increasingly clear to me that real, positive change for our neighbourhoods requires a fresh approach and a political home that puts fairness, community action, and the local environment at the heart of everything “Joining the Green Party is not a decision taken lightly or out of frustration with others, but out of a genuine belief that it offers the most constructive and community-focused path forward “My focus on the ground will not change, I will continue to work tirelessly for our residents every single day, and I remain committed to working collaboratively with colleagues across all parties for the good of Bolton .”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Carrington Relief Road: Hundreds of objections, £132 million, and just 15-years until it hits capacity The Carrington Relief Road is a very expensive, hugely controversial plan that campaigners say will cause 'severe and permanent harm', but Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 19:30, 11 Oct 2026 The controversial Carrington Relief Road comes with a whopping £132m price tag, but parts will be operating near capacity within just 15 years, documents show The relief road has been touted by political leaders as the solution to traffic woes in the area around Partington and Carrington . The project aims to divert traffic away from the A6144, reducing congestion and improving travel times for drivers and public transport users But traffic modelling data published by Trafford council reveals that by 2045 two sections of the route, including a key junction, will hit more than 90pc capacity – the point at which severe congestion is thought to be highly probable. The road is not expected to open until afte The 2.7-mile road would link the A6144 Manchester Road to the west with the A6144 Carrington Spur in the east. He is described as a white man, aged approximately in his 50s, with short brown hair and a grey beard." In the aftermath, Hall was taken to hospital and his blood was tested for alcohol, giving a reading of 77 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport European airline set to cancel Manchester Airport flights due to strike action Around 140 flights could be cancelled at Brussels Airport on Friday Add to preferred sources Comments News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 12:19, 07 Oct 2026 V Flights between Brussels and Manchester Airport could be disrupted on Friday due to strike action by ground handler Alyzia. Around 140 flights arriving and departing from Brussels Airport on October 9 could be cancelled due to national strike action according to local media In a statement on its website, Brussels Airport said: “On Friday 9 October there is a national manifestation. Part of the staff from ground handler Alyzia is expected to take part in this action. Based on the current information approximately half of the flights handled by Alyzia The airport added that passengers would be contacted directly. It said their website would be updated to show cancellations only once they are registered by the airline and it apologised for any inconvenience caused Alyzia handles airline operations for several large airlines flying to and from Brussels, including Brussels Airlines, The Brussels Times reports. The airline operates four flights between Manchester Airport which could be impacted These are flights from Brussels to Manchester at 10am and 9.30pm, and two flights from Manchester to Brussels, departing at 8.30am and 1.30pm. Flights operated by other airlines including Ryanair, easyJet and British Airways are not affected as their ground handling is dealt with

Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes A community group fears plans to build homes next to a nature reserve could destroy a Stockport ‘gem’ forever. This week councillors considered plans for 181 new homes to be built off Jacksons Lane in Hazel Grove It is the latest plan put forward for consideration in the area after 160 homes were approved last month. The new plans promise to provide 91 homes that will be classed as affordable with 20 for social rent. The development would be entirely within the green belt and close to the The plans include funds for new open space as well as a £30,000 contribution to support nature within the reserve. There is also a promised £1.3m contribution towards education provision and £243,608 towards creating additional floorspace at possible three different medical centr However Deborah Hind, on behalf of the Friends of Happy Valley, said she was worried about the plan’s impact on the area and its wildlife which she was a ‘massive asset’ to the borough. If the plans are approved, she feared increased footfall would degrade the area over time She added: “We are about to devastate such an asset, such a gem in Stockport and I sound quite emotional because that’s what I am, because I just can’t believe that we’re allowing another development and people are going to walk down into that valley.”

Fortunately, the victim only needed stitches Law-Glindon was hauled before a judge this week for sentencing having previously admitted a charge of wounding. Recorder Imran Shafi KC told him: "Your actions that day were absolutely disgraceful. You behaved like an animal, which is doing a disservice to most animals." Following the hearing, Law-Glindon - who has dice tattooed on his hand - was pictured holding a lottery scratchcard after escaping an immediate prison sentence

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Four suspects named after police storm six Rochdale homes in £1m raids Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group raided six properties after a six-month investigation News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 09:54, 05 Oct 20 Four men have been charged after police seized a huge drugs haul worth around £1 million in raids in Rochdale Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit, executed six warrants across the town on September 28. The force said the swoops followed a six month-long probe into a 'suspected large-scale supply and distribution of illicit drugs' One of the properties raided was on on Manchester Road in Rochdale. Police said there they found a 'vast quantity' of suspected class A, B and C drugs, worth around £1 million at street value, as well as a large number of electronic devices and £60,00 in cash Four men have since been charged following the raids. The four men are: Jalil Ahmed, 52, of Twinegate, Rochdale, Shakil Ahmed, 23, of Twinegate, Rochdale, Shakil Ahmed, 51, of Whittaker Lane, Rochdale, and Raja Adeel Farooq, 44, of Kingsway, Manchester Jalil Ahmed, 23-year-old Shakil Ahmed and 51-year-old Shakil Ahmed have all been charged with conspiracy to supply class A, B and C drugs, supplying medicine products and money laundering

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Gang used cruel cash machine trick to steal thousands from pensioners The three men would work together to distract their 'vulnerable' targets Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:49, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Three members of an organised crime gang have been jailed after they stole thousands of pounds from pensioners across the country using a cruel trick at cash machines Ionut Matei, 40, Vasile Ciubotaru, 45, and Ramonel Mandache, 51, together stole more than £40,000 from their 'vulnerable' victims. The trio targeted people using ATMs in Halifax bank, including in the Stockport and Bury branches, and at Lloyds Bank Detectives found Matei, Ciubotaru and Mandache, who are all Romanian nationals, would travel across the country during their malicious enterprise. To trick their victims, one of the men would stand close enough to see them entering their pin into the cash machine Another would distract them by drawing attention to a banknote deliberately placed on the floor nearby, Cheshire Police said. The third man would then swipe their bank card and replace it with a similar-looking card Victims were left completely unaware that their card had been stolen. The gang would then use the stolen cards and PIN to withdraw cash and buy items, often before the victims had realised what had happened

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamorous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 11:51, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hous A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamorous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The hero firefighter who died trying to save a life More than 25 years after Sub Officer Paul Metcalf died trying to rescue a teenager from Hawkshaw's Simons Lodge, an FBU Red Plaque at Ramsbottom Fire Station honours the hero whose sacrifice transfor News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:43, 27 Sep 2026 Updated 17:00, 27 Sep 2026 It was an act of heroism which ended in tragedy. But every firefighter in the UK owes a debt to Paul Metcalf who died trying in vain to save the life of a teenager On a balmy autumn Sunday in 1999 Sub Officer Metcalf, based at Ramsbottom Fire Station and a crew answered a call. A boy had vanished under the surface at Simons Lodge, Hawkshaw. He had slipped into the water from a rope swing hanging from a tree as he tested the temperature with Super fit Mr Metcalf, aged 40, and a karate black belt, dived in but his non-floating rope became snagged on an underwater branch. As colleagues and police pulled the line to bring him ashore, unaware it was caught, he was pulled under water Despite the valiant efforts of two colleagues to save him it took 15 minutes to recover him and he died soon after in hospital But the legacy of Paul's death was that it led directly to the introduction of water safety and rescue equipment on frontline fire appliances nationally and the replacement of traditional hemp lines with floating nylon line

The tightknit neighbourhood jokingly describes itself as ‘a community of curtain-twitchers’. Really, it’s a place where people stop to chat on front porches, There’s just one major issue facing these neighbours: the recycling plant at the bottom of their road For years, residents claim they’ve been plagued by noise, bad smells, as well as rat and seagull infestations. Simon Richardson denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources A murder trial has heard of the tragic injuries Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins suffered after he was struck by a car and dragged for over a mile before dying at the side of he road Simon Richardson, 35, is alleged to have murdered Michael Mullins as he cycled home in April this year. Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving and is on trial at Minshull Street Crown Court Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham on April 20. The 56-year-old headteacher was making his way home to Northwich after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, the court was told He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm. Mr Richardson, 35, earlier failed to properly observe a junction, 'flying straight through the give way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins, it is alleged Jurors heard that the defendant didn't stop and 'put his foot down'. Mr Mullins was trapped under the car while his damaged bike was left in the road

It was 3.30am on a 'cold and miserable' October morning. A young Pat had arrived i "It looked horrible to me and I wanted to go 'home'," he once wrote in the Manchester Evening News . "Six months later we were happy as can be in Harpurhey and all the family fell in love with Manchester which had given us a home." Pat went on to devote his life to the city and its people. That bleak landscape of late-industrial Manchester Pat first saw in the 1950s would be utterly unrecognisable by the time the shattering news of his death was announced this week , aged 78 He played his own significant role in that transformation, becoming the face of the city centre and a fierce champion of its growth. Famously, he was also Manchester's 'Mr Christmas', who would happily keep the festive markets open all year round if he had his way But in a political career spanning almost half a century, Pat's influence and legacy spans well beyond the glitz of the city centre. The 25-year-old man is suspected of 'acting as a negotiator' between an alleged criminal group and its victims, police said He was due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court in London on Thursday (October 1) for an extradition hearing, although the Eastern Region Special Operations Unit (ERSOU), a specialist policing unit involved in the operation in the UK, hasn't specified a country Ransomware networks are criminal operations which threaten organisations with the release of stolen files unless a ransom is paid. Multiple arrests were made across Europe in coordinated strikes on Wednesday A statement from the ERSOU said police from its specialist cyber-crime unit joined law enforcement agencies from nine countries to arrest 'suspected members of an alleged organised criminal gang and seize infrastructure linked to KillSec' Active since around 2024, KillSec was described by police as a dark web leak site 'used to extort victims and publish stolen data'. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport The millions councils have made from Manchester Airport Some councillors want more Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 08:03, 17 Oct 2026 View Image Terminal 2 at Manchester Airport departur Councils across the region raked made in £318m from Manchester Airport s Group in three years after payments stopping during the Covid-19 pandemic In recent years, some councillors and town hall bosses across the region have asked for major payments to start up again from the Manchester Airport Group, which owns Manchester, East Midlands, and London Stansted airports. There were further calls this week as finance chiefs at Manchester Airports Group (MAG) is 64.5 per cent owned by the 10 Greater Manchester authorities with Manchester City Council being the biggest investor with 34.5pc. The city council’s leader sits is a director and the region’s nine other councils hold 29pc of shares between them The airport group is privately managed despite the 10 local authorities owning a majority of shares between them and 30pc of shares are held by IFM Investors As a result of council investment in the airport group in 1986, Greater Manchester councils have received dividends in the past on the profits made. Officers found huge quantities of crystal methamphetamine and ketamine, as well as a 20-litre barrel containing a chemical believed to be used in the enhancement of the drugs Two men were arrested, including Cairo Taylor, 29, who was later charged and pleaded guilty to 16 offences relating to the supply of drugs. The items were recovered by Greater Manchester Police before being passed on to Royal Mail Officers discovered the items after searching the property following an arrest in connection with a separate offence this summer, the Manchester Evening News understands. The number of items found was confirmed to be between 10,000 and 11,000 It's understood that the worker involved, who is believed to have been employed by Royal Mail in Bury for a number of years, is no longer with the business. Royal Mail has not confirmed whether the matter has been referred to police for a criminal investigation The M.E.N. understands each item of mail currently being held by Royal Mail will be delivered to its rightful recipient, along with a covering letter explaining the circumstances. Since being handed over to Royal Mail by police, the mail has been kept at the Bury delivery office, It has since been sorted by delivery area and is now being prepared for delivery, it is understood. Some of the items recovered are believed to have been damaged or tampered with in some way

The 24-year-old simply texted him the life-changing news "I guess some people might find it odd, but Rachel and I never had that conversation," said Harry, 22. "She never asked if I wanted her kidney and I never asked to have it. She spoke to my mum about it and just texted me saying she wanted to do it." The siblings say they have always been close, but when Harry became seriously ill while studying at university in London, that "special bond" took on a new significance. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Homelessness The people risking their lives for change at Greater Manchester's busy junctions More people seem to be asking for money on hectic roads than before View 5 Images More people have been seen begging for change at Manchester's busiest junct Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 05:30, 11 Oct 2026 Updated 07:34, 11 Oct 2026 Drive around some of Greater Manchester's busiest roads at peak times and there's a good chance you'll be asked for change. Begging at some of the region's busiest junction But it seems to have become more common in recent months, across more of the region's roads. Those involved are often putting themselves at risk People are regularly seen walking past queues of traffic asking for money, or sitting at traffic islands between hectic crossroads. The majority of the cases, 38, have taken place in Salford , but two further reports have been received in Stockport , Greater Manchester Police said in an update And the force said the 'vast majority' of the cases are now being treated as racially or religiously-motivated The windows of homes suspected of being 'houses of multiple occupation' have been smashed, with graffiti daubed on walls. But police said properties mistaken for HMOs have also targeted, as they revealed social media posts are also being monitored by an investigation team In a statement, GMP said: "Our investigation into a spate of criminal damage offences is progressing as we work closely with partners to crack down on the offending "Since 5 October, we have received 40 reports of criminal damage at properties – which include HMOs. We also believe properties mistaken for HMOs are being targeted. A total of 38 of the offences under investigation have been committed in Salford."

Part of Heywood Road was blocked off last month after a huge stretch of tarmac started to buckle . Investigations revealed the cause to be a burst sewer pipe, But the disruption is not over for motorists , with road closures now extended to the roundabout junction with Heys Road. These are expected to be in place for up to two weeks, a spokeswoman for United Utilities has said During this time, ‘proactive’ works will be undertaken to ‘future-proof’ the sewer network in the area. This will involve replacing additional sections of pipe and reinforcing these with lining. Once this is complete, footpaths along the route will also be reinstated, the spokesw The company hopes the work will go some way to reducing further incidents of this nature. The town has seen sinkhole after sinkhole open under its roads in recent years This is because Prestwich is largely built on sand. Officers from the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit swooped on the home of Jacob Naylor, of Huddersfield Road in Staly In a search warrant they seized two 3D printed firearms, plastic and metal firearms parts, 9mm rounds and a 3D printer, as well as a bag of cannabis Together with the Metropolitan Police’s Forensic Firearms Unit, the force established that the two firearms were a FGC-9 and a 'DIY' AR9 made from plastic and metal pressured parts. The 9mm were not live rounds The AR9 was found to be missing some components and was not useable, but the FGC-9 was found to be capable of firing bullets and being used as a firearm Naylor's DNA was found on both the printer and the firearms, with instructions and codes detailing how to manufacture and assemble the firearms found on the printer SD card

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation Officers also recovered cash, stolen goods and illicit drugs Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:28, 07 Oct 2026 View Image A Three men have been arrested as part of a seven-month investigation into a drug dealing network. Officers from Greater Manchester Police and West Midlands Police carried out two raids in Wolverhampton on Wednesday morning (October 7) As well as the arrests, the operation led to the discovery of large quantities of illegal drugs, stolen vehicles and cash The search of an address on Penn Road saw a man in his 60s arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply controlled drugs, he remains in police custody. Officers also seized approximately £1,000 in cash and around 50 Class C tablets At the second address on Stephen Close, a teenager was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and theft of a motor vehicle. A woman in her 40s was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and child endangerment The pair remain in custody. Police say around 2,000 Class B tablets and a stolen motorcycle were seized at the property, with officers also finding blister packs in a baby’s cot

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Metrolink Three Metrolink lines will close for two weeks from tomorrow Passengers are being warned of disruption Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 11:50, 18 Oct 2026 View Image Work to replace tracks along a 4km stretch arounsd Tr Three Metrolink lines are to close for fortnight from tomorrow (Monday) for engineering works on one of the busiest stretches of tram line in Europe. Deansgate-Castlefield, Cornbrook and Trafford Bar stations will shut until Monday, November 2, Transport for Greater Manchester (T The two-week closure will mean there will be no trams running on the Altrincham , Trafford Centre and Eccles lines. Meanwhile the station closures will also mean services to East Didsbury and Manchester Airport will end at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will stop at Exchange S The impacted stretch is ‘one of the busiest in Europe’ with trams passing through every 30 seconds for 20 hours a day, seven days a week. TfGM said the work will allow further speed restrictions along the line to be lifted, making journeys ‘quicker and more reliable’ Match-going United and City fans are also being warned the closures could affect them. City are due to host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday, Brighton in the Carabao Cup on October 28, and the same opponents in the Premier League on October 31 Meanwhile, United will take on Bournemouth at Old Trafford on October 25 in the Premier League. The works will see around 4km of track replaced as part of a wider £150m project

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Middleton Unlicensed teen taught himself to drive on YouTube, ran red lights, then killed beloved dad in Middleton horror crash Ruhul Islam was sentenced to six years and 11 months in prison following the death of Terence James View 4 Images Ruhul Isl Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 17:13, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 22:36, 14 Oct 2026 An unlicensed teenager who taught himself to drive by watching YouTube videos swerved through traffic and ran red lights before ploughing his older brother's Terence James , 78, died after being struck by the vehicle on Shawbury Street, Middleton , on September 29, 2024. Yesterday (October 13), Manchester Crown Court heard how Ruhul Islam had borrowed the car to make takeaway deliveries at the time of the offence The 16-year-old was seen overtaking and undertaking vehicles, running red lights and weaving between lanes in the moments before the crash Now 18, he has been jailed for nearly seven years. Passing sentence, Judge Kate Cornell said: "The vehicle essentially became a dangerous weapon in the hands of someone unable to use it." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Northern 'Unreliable' Northern trains could be a thing of the past if Greater Manchester gets its way If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region. Comments News Edward Barnes Northern Rail’s ‘ageing’ and ‘unreliable’ trains could soon be a thing of the past if Manchester transport bosses get their way Northern is currently bidding for funding which would see the rail operator’s largest ever investment in its fleet. If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region If approved, the new trains would be introduced on a phased basis, replacing the oldest units in the fleet, most of which have been in service since the 1980s and 90s. Approximately two thirds of the existing fleet is targeted to be replaced in the next ten years According to Northern’s website, they hope to award contracts in 2027 with the first trains delivered by 2030. A total of 130 new trains would be delivered as part of phase one over three years replacing trains at or near ‘the end of their life’ An update was given on the major investment plan at a recent Bee Network committee meeting following questions on transport issues across Greater Manchester

The expansion responds to increasing demand for specialist school places and will enable more children and young people to have their needs met closer to home The new facilities allow Millwood to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with a range of additional educational needs and disabilities, providing high-quality learning environments designed to support pupils to thrive and achieve their full potential

Funded to the tune of £2.2m by Arts Council England, 18-19 Market Place sits within Stockport’s historic core. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia
